sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LiteLLM is an open-source AI gateway and Python SDK that lets you call 100+ LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and Azure, using the OpenAI request format. Use it as a library in your code or run it as a central proxy for your team.
sixtySeconds.problem: Every LLM provider has its own SDK, auth, request format and errors. LiteLLM gives you one interface, so you can switch providers without rewriting code, and its gateway adds virtual keys, spend tracking, guardrails and load balancing.
whoFor: ML platform teams giving staff one LLM endpoint
Companies tracking LLM spend per team or user
Apps that need fallbacks between providers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a widely used, self-hosted way to standardise and govern LLM access. Some enterprise features are under a separate commercial license.
requirements: API keys for the providers you use
Docker for production deployments (stable images use the -stable tag)

overview: The Python SDK exposes completion() and other functions that accept any supported model name, such as openai/... or anthropic/..., with the same OpenAI-style messages. A Router adds retries, fallbacks and load balancing across deployments, and auto routing can choose a model per prompt.

The AI Gateway (proxy server) is a central service your apps call with the regular OpenAI SDK pointed at it. It provides authentication, virtual keys, per-project and per-user spend tracking, guardrails, caching, logging and an admin dashboard. The README reports 8 ms P95 latency at 1,000 requests per second in its benchmarks.

Supported endpoints include chat completions, responses, embeddings, images, audio, batches, rerank, the A2A agent protocol and Anthropic-style messages. It can also act as an MCP gateway. Terraform modules deploy it on AWS or GCP. Code under litellm/enterprise has its own license; the rest is MIT.

steps.title: Call any provider
steps.code:
from litellm import completion
import os

os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = "your-anthropic-key"
response = completion(model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}])

steps.title: Start it
steps.body: It serves an OpenAI-compatible API on port 4000.

firstRun.title: Call the gateway with the OpenAI SDK
firstRun.code:
import openai
client = openai.OpenAI(api_key="anything", base_url="http://0.0.0.0:4000")
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-6.1-sol",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
